summary: Coverage is healthy on churn and pricing and empty on partner proof for the third week running — that pillar is 25% of the plan and has produced nothing because we still don't have Dana's amplify list. Two strong signals this week: a benchmark report she can argue with, and an EU pricing-disclosure rule that makes her pricing argument suddenly time-bound.

rows.pillar: Why customers quit in week one

signals.pillar: Why customers quit in week one
signals.what: A widely-shared onboarding benchmark report claims median time-to-value of 14 days across B2B SaaS — a figure that doesn't match what Dana sees in her own cohort data.
signals.why_buyers_care: Heads of onboarding are already being handed this number by their boards as a target.
signals.our_angle: Dana has 40 implementations' worth of data saying the median is meaningfully worse and the average hides the failure mode. Disagreeing with a number in public, with your own number, is the most citable thing you can do.
signals.proof: Cohort study across 40 implementations (18% figure cleared)

signals.what: An EU disclosure rule taking effect in Q1 forces published price ranges for a class of software contracts.
signals.why_buyers_care: Anyone selling into the EU has a deadline now, and most of them hide pricing today.
signals.our_angle: Dana already did this voluntarily and has the before/after. 'We did this two years ago and here's what actually happened' is the post every one of those companies will search for.
signals.proof: 2025 pricing publication — needs her OK on the win-rate delta

signals.pillar: Why customers quit in week one
signals.what: A long r/CustomerSuccess thread this week: 'our activation numbers look fine but customers churn at month three' — 90+ comments, no good answer.
signals.why_buyers_care: It is her exact buyer asking her exact question in public, in their own words.
signals.our_angle: Dana's view that vanity activation metrics mask the real leading indicator — she can name the three that actually predict it.

signals.what: The pricing consultant who owns this topic posted a framework for 'when not to publish pricing' that got heavy engagement.
signals.why_buyers_care: It's the counter-argument her buyers will have read before they read her.
signals.our_angle: Not a rebuttal — a concession post. Where he's right, where her own data disagreed, and what she'd do differently. Steelmanning the other side is what makes a practitioner citable rather than partisan.

signals.pillar: Why customers quit in week one
signals.what: A competitor shipped an 'onboarding health score' feature and is posting about it from the company page only.
signals.why_buyers_care: Buyers will ask whether a score is a real signal or a dashboard ornament.
signals.our_angle: Dana's opinion on what a health score gets wrong when nobody owns the follow-up. Their post is on a company page; hers would be on a profile — that's the citation gap.
